title: Stanisław Poniatowski's letters to Charles XII from the Porte: French number cipher with interlinear decipherment
correspondents: Stanisław Poniatowski (major general in Swedish service, the King's agent at the Ottoman court) -> Charles XII
language: French (2-3 digit number code mixed with clear words)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/5/8 (Generalmajoren Stanislaus Poniatowski, 1710-1714)
folio_note: 437 images (series 40006063). Cipher with French decipherment between the lines at images 274, 310 and 328 (whole pages); only 24 of 437 images sampled.
status: Catalogue: "Generalmajoren Stanislaus Poniatowski", no mention of cipher. Sampled pages carry long runs of number groups with the French plaintext written above them by the recipient's clerk.
why: The King's chief negotiator at the Porte during the Bender exile (Prut campaign, 1711 peace, the Kalabalik); his ciphered reports with their decipherments give a key and a dated series.
verify: Page the volume and list every ciphered letter; rebuild the code from the interlinear pairs; check whether Poniatowski's code is the Funck/Perman field-chancery code (groups like 135, 61, 87 recur in both).

title: Bender field-chancery number code: Funck, Perman and von Müllern despatches with interlinear decipherments
correspondents: Thomas Funck (envoy at the Porte) -> Charles XII and the Kanslikollegium; commission secretary Hans Perman -> H. G. von Müllern; von Müllern -> Funck
language: Swedish and French (2-3 digit number code)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/6/9, I/6/10, I/6/14 and I/7/16 (Funck to the King 1710-13; to the Kanslikollegium 1711-13; from von Müllern 1711-13; Perman to von Müllern 1711-14)
folio_note: I/6/9: 536 images (40006064), image 335. I/6/10: 98 images (40006065), images 58, 66, 70, 86. I/6/14: 235 images (40006068), images 69-70 (Müllern to Funck 20 Aug 1711). I/7/16: 153 images (40006070), images 20, 33, 39, 45, 71, 77 (whole pages). Drafts in clear: I/6/11 (523 images) and I/6/12 (541).
status: Catalogue says nothing of cipher. The same groups recur in all four volumes (290, 504, 204, 664, 746, 891), each with the decipherment written between the lines (Swedish; French letter by letter in I/6/14). Catalogue #1769 (Funck I/6/13, the King's letters to Funck) is this code without glosses.
why: Charles XII's secret correspondence from Bender with his envoys at the Porte, 1710-14. The glossed pages give the key for #1769 and for any other unglossed despatch of the exile years.
verify: Collect the interlinear pairs from I/7/16 (densest), rebuild the code, then apply it to #1769 (I/6/13). Fold this lead into #1769 as its key material if the editor prefers one entry per key.

title: Clas Rålamb's despatches from Constantinople: number cipher with interlinear decipherment
correspondents: Clas Rålamb and Gotthard Vellingk (envoys extraordinary) -> Charles X Gustav
language: Swedish (number code, groups 1-110 and a few in the 800s)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/2/2 (E.o. ablegaterna Clas Rålamb och Gotthard Vellingk, 1657)
folio_note: 132 images (series 40008933). Cipher at image 23 (two pages of number runs with Swedish between the lines) and image 88 (letter of 12 June 1657 signed Clas Rålamb).
status: Catalogue: the volume title only. Rålamb's embassy is well studied (his diary, ed. Callmer 1963; the Rålamb paintings), but no account of his ciphers was found. A different code from the 1711 Funck code.
why: The Swedish embassy to Mehmed IV in 1657-58, sent to bind Transylvania into Charles X's Polish war; its ciphered reports and their decipherments give a dated 1650s Swedish chancery code.
verify: Page the volume for every cipher passage; rebuild the code from the interlinear pairs; compare with the Rákóczi cipher of 2119.5/4 (lead 2243) and Cantersten 1648.

title: Consul J. A. Molinari's despatches from Tunis: unglossed number cipher in unbroken digit strings
correspondents: Johan Adam Molinari (Swedish consul at Tunis) -> the Kanslipresident (Stockholm)
language: French (cipher text numeric, digits run together without separators)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, bihang Tunisica, SE/RA/2119/2119.7/2 (Svenska konsulers skrivelser, J. A. Molinari, 1764-1778)
folio_note: 732 images (series R0003585). Image 123: letter of Tunis 21 March 1765, a page of digit strings ending in clear French; image 366: letter of 7 July 1770, two pages of digit strings, clear close; image 153 looks the same. Only 24 of 732 images sampled.
status: Catalogue: consuls' letters, J. A. Molinari; no mention of cipher. The sampled cipher pages carry no decipherment. The digits are written continuously, so the group length must be found first (likely 2- or 3-digit groups).
why: Sweden's consul at Tunis during the 1760s crises with the Regency and the Mediterranean passport system; an unglossed 18th-century consular code, a ciphertext-only target.
verify: Page the volume for every cipher letter and any decipherment or key slip; look for the Kanslikollegium's consular code of the 1760s (Riksarkivet chiffer collections); measure digit-string lengths for the group size.
